entries.name: THE ROAD BACK TO MAIN STREET

LOOK_AT.line: The road back up to Main Street, where the lamps are closer together and the mud is better dressed.

LISTEN_TO.line: Main Street, a little way off. The Nugget, mostly.

LOOK_AT.line: The Claims Registrar's, with a light in the window every time I have walked past. The paperwork does not sleep.

LISTEN_TO.line: Through the door, a stamp, then a pen, then the stamp again.

LOOK_AT.line: A gap between the Registrar's and the church, going round the back of everything.

LISTEN_TO.line: The alley, breathing cold air out between the buildings.

LOOK_AT.line: Double doors up the steps, and a bell hung on a post beside them, at a height for ringing by hand.

LISTEN_TO.line: Inside, a hymnal's pages turning, or the draft turning them for nobody.

LOOK_AT.line: A passage through to the Lane, where the undertaker and the medium keep each other in business.

LISTEN_TO.line: Small bells, from the far end: the tent flap, letting somebody out.

LOOK_AT.line: The livery's doors, open a man's width, with a lamp inside and straw spilling out to meet the mud.

LISTEN_TO.line: Hooves shifting on straw, and a mule saying something short.

LOOK_AT.line: The road out of town, to the claims. Every man in Consolation walks it in the morning and back at night, and only the mornings are hopeful.

LISTEN_TO.line: The wind coming down from the diggings, with a loose board knocking somewhere along the way.

LOOK_AT.line: The Claims Registrar's window, lit.
Somewhere behind the glare is a man who has never once been surprised.

LISTEN_TO.line: A pen, scratching, then a long pause, then a stamp.
The rhythm of a form being found incomplete.

LOOK_AT.line: A water trough with a skin of dust on it and a square of night sky in the middle.

LISTEN_TO.line: A slow drip from the seam, keeping its own time.

LOOK_AT.line: A bell on a post by the church steps, with a dent where the mallet lands.
It was cast to a note, and it has been coming down off it ever since.

LISTEN_TO.line: It hums when the wind catches it. Even humming, it's low.

LOOK_AT.line: The livery stable. The doors stand open on a lantern and a heap of hay.
The horses are further in, out of sight and, from the sound of them, out of patience.

LISTEN_TO.line: Horses, shifting their weight and their opinions.

LOOK_AT.line: The church, which on weekdays is the meeting hall and on most days is neither.
The whitest thing in town, because it is the only thing anyone repaints.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing from inside. The pews are holding their breath for Sunday.

LOOK_AT.line: Main Street's mud, continued. Out here it has stopped trying to impress anyone.

LISTEN_TO.line: Quieter than Main Street. The piano is a rumor from here.

LOOK_AT.line: The door out. It has a bell on a spring that announces everyone.

LISTEN_TO.line: The street.

LOOK_AT.line: A brass bell on the counter, the kind you strike with the flat of your hand.
It is the only thing in this office that answers at once.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. A bell that isn't being rung is a bell at its best.

LOOK_AT.line: The territorial statutes, bound in black, thick as a family Bible and consulted more often.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. A closed book of statutes is the quietest thing a government makes.

LOOK_AT.line: The claims ledger. Every filing in the district, in one book, in one hand.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing.

LOOK_AT.line: A stack of Form 12-C, squared to the edge of the counter.
It is the form a claim is made of, and the stack has never once run low.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. Paper this well squared doesn't make a sound.

LOOK_AT.line: A pen, chained to the counter. The chain is longer than the counter requires.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing.

LOOK_AT.line: A spindle of numbered tickets. I'm ninety-one.
There's one other man in the room, and he's forty.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. It waits extremely well.

LOOK_AT.line: The office clock. It is authoritative and it is wrong.

LISTEN_TO.line: Running eleven minutes fast. I know because the church bell disagrees with it, and the church bell is half a step flat.

LOOK_AT.line: A door, locked, with a statute posted beside it explaining precisely who may pass through. I am not among them.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. It is very thick and there is nothing behind it that moves.

LOOK_AT.line: Forms in triplicate, and a sign explaining that the third copy is for the applicant.
There is no third copy in any of the slots.

LISTEN_TO.line: Paper, settling. It is a sound like a very slow argument.

LOOK_AT.line: Every claim in the district, pinned and numbered.
Claim One is a rectangle like all the others.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing.

LOOK_AT.line: A bench along the wall for those waiting. It seats nine.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing.

LOOK_AT.line: A counter built a little too high to lean on comfortably. I've tested this. Repeatedly.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing.

LOOK_AT.line: Two roped lines, two signs. FILING and INQUIRIES.
There is nobody in either of them and the ropes are up regardless.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. Two empty queues are quieter than one.

LOOK_AT.line: A wooden partition from the counter to the ceiling, posts and rails, with the clerk's side behind it. It is built like a bank's, to guard a room full of paper.

LISTEN_TO.line: The office on the far side, a little quieter than the office on this side.
It is the same air. It has been told which side it's on.

LOOK_AT.line: The road out to the coach stop, the same way I came in, the other way round.

LISTEN_TO.line: The road, quiet, the way roads are before anybody has had an opinion about them.

LOOK_AT.line: Under all the claims and disputes, one new notice, official, sealed, correctly spelled. It has the whole board's attention.

LISTEN_TO.line: Paper in wind. This morning it sounds like applause. I'm aware that's me.

LOOK_AT.line: Three inches of water, and this morning, the whole sky in it.

LISTEN_TO.line: The thing that lives in it, surfacing. We have both made it through.

LOOK_AT.line: The dog, in the early sun, in the middle of the street, on his back.
He has always known something the rest of us are only learning this morning.

LISTEN_TO.line: Breathing. Contented. The town's oldest solvency, undiluted.

LOOK_AT.line: The tallest thing in Consolation, catching the first light, as is its habit and its right.

LISTEN_TO.line: The bell. In tune. Sowerby has not changed how he strikes it.
Nothing changed but everything under it.

LOOK_AT.line: The gilt is peeling off the lettering in the morning sun.
Nobody will repaint it now, and the sign has the good grace to know it.

LISTEN_TO.line: It creaks. It would like to be taken down. I know another sign that felt that way.

LOOK_AT.line: Six inches above the mud, same as ever. The distinction matters less this morning.
Everyone is walking in the middle of the street anyway.

LISTEN_TO.line: The loose board, third from the end. Still loose. Somebody should see to that.
It will outlast us all.

LOOK_AT.line: The hills, gone gold at the top — the ordinary kind, the kind the sun hands out free every morning and nobody ever had to dig for.

LISTEN_TO.line: Very faint, and for the first time since I stepped off the coach: no picks.
The hills, being left alone.

LOOK_AT.line: The same mud. It held my boot the first night and the truth the whole time.
The only honest thing in the territory, as I believe I remarked.

LISTEN_TO.line: Nothing. It never once lied to me. Even now it declines to start.

LOOK_AT.line: The same two-story faces on the same one-story buildings — but at dawn, with the light behind them, they look like what they always were: a promise somebody kept badly and everybody kept anyway.

LISTEN_TO.line: Wind behind them, same as ever. It sounds less empty than it did. That may be me.
